push_headlines: Europe had its worst day in eight months: the STOXX 600 -1.75% to 650.72 on AI jitters before Nvidia's results.
Asia slid on new US curbs on China's access to AI chips: the Nikkei 225 -1.18% near 58,960 and the Hang Seng -0.77% near 23,570.
Oil eased on surplus forecasts: Brent -0.70% to $91.80 and WTI near $85.20.
on_notice: Nvidia reports after Tuesday's close under interim CEO Colette Kress, so Nasdaq 100 futures may swing overnight.
Washington said it will tighten China's access to advanced AI chips, which hit Asian chipmakers; watch whether Seoul and Taipei extend losses Wednesday.
Tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz are offsetting the surplus story in oil, so a fresh incident could reverse Tuesday's dip.

asia.headline: Tokyo and Seoul fell as tech sold off on new US chip curbs and Nvidia nerves.
asia.detail: The Nikkei 225 -1.18% near 58,960 in Tuesday trade, led down by Kioxia, Advantest and SoftBank Group. The Kospi -2.00% shortly after the open and Taiwan shares -1.40%. No verified closing levels for Seoul or Taipei were found.

china.headline: Hong Kong gave back Monday's gain as tech led the decline; no verified Shanghai close was found.
china.detail: The Hang Seng -0.77% near 23,570 and the Hang Seng Tech index about -2.00%, as the US move to tighten China's access to advanced AI chips weighed on the sector. Searches returned no citable Shanghai Composite level for Tuesday.

europe.headline: The STOXX 600 had its worst day in eight months on AI jitters, with Deutsche Bank sliding.
europe.detail: The STOXX 600 -1.75% to 650.72, its biggest one-day drop since March 20, leaving it 2.5% below last week's record high. Tech led the selling ahead of Nvidia's results. No confirmed DAX or FTSE 100 close was found.

latam.headline: No Ibovespa close for Tuesday was found.
latam.detail: Searches returned no Rio Times or B3 report for Tuesday's session, so no Brazilian level is quoted here.

mideast.headline: Oil eased on surplus forecasts, with Hormuz tanker attacks limiting the drop.
mideast.detail: Brent -0.70% to $91.80 and WTI near $85.20, per HDFC Sky, as the IEA's view of a fourth-quarter surplus and recovering Gulf exports weighed. OilPrice.com reported tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz offsetting part of that pressure, with Brent stuck near $93.00 in US morning trade.
